state_authority: Existing application CORE_DB job checkpoint; actors have no database or policy-write authority
execution: One to eight actual spawned local actor processes run isolated pinned environments against one frozen policy per batch. Parent validates bounded JSON IPC, then performs sequential actual Q updates and episode-atomic commits. No mutable Q table or thread is shared with actors.
binding: Exact environment request/spec, full frozen policy snapshot/digest, implementation/runtime identity, actor count, fixed episode ordinals/seeds, logical actor IDs and per-actor rollout RNG. Physical actor PID/channel is checked by issuing parent.
checkpoint: Persist pending batch before spawning; each commit atomically stores updated policy, complete trace and acknowledged prefix. Recovery pins frozen batch policy and skips acknowledged episodes, recollecting only uncommitted deterministic episodes. Central learner snapshot remains authoritative.
frames: Bounded actual environment previews carry batch/actor/assignment/policy/environment/step identities; frames are live observations and do not imply an episode or policy commit.
cleanup: Cooperative cancellation, bounded wait, then terminate/kill/join every spawned actor; POSIX process groups include nested approved emulator workers. If the OS cannot reap a killed process within the bounded cleanup waits, retain its handle in execution quarantine, reject new actors, and report cleanup_not_quiescent without claiming completion. No surviving child is acknowledged as a successful return.
measured_evidence: Actor traces are admitted only from the actual parent-created process channel with complete assignment and trace validation; uploaded issuer labels cannot grant measured-actor provenance.
limits: Local process parallel rollout collection, not remote training, neural distributed optimization or guaranteed throughput. Frozen-batch collection differs numerically from online action selection after each Q update; resume equivalence is to the same batch algorithm.
